Subject: Clarification: token packaging, seat bundles, and monthly true-up

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we finalize the pilot SOW we'd like a written clarification on a few billing mechanics so Procurement and Finance can sign off:

1) Token accounting: do you bill both prompt (input) and completion (output) tokens? If a single API call has a 2,000-token prompt and 300-token generated answer, how will that appear on the invoice?

2) Context-length handling: if we store a long doc and query a 1,000-token slice, are we charged for the entire 32k doc ingest or only the returned/windowed portion?

3) Rounding and minimums: what is the billing quantum (e.g., 100/250/500 tokens)? Is there a per-request minimum and a monthly minimum for low-volume pilots?

I've attached a usage sample for our expected pilot traffic so you can run concrete examples. We'd like the answers in time for our internal review on Friday.

Attachment: acme_usage_sample_q1.csv (text/csv, 12K)

Thanks,
Lara Chen

AcmeHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification: token packaging, seat bundles, and monthly true-up

Lara —

Great questions, and thanks for the sample. Below are our standard rules plus a couple of pilot-friendly concessions we can put in the SOW. I included worked examples attached (token_amortization_examples.pdf) and a proposed pricing table (proposed_pricing_table_v2.xlsx).

Short answers up front:
- Token accounting: billed for both input + output (total tokens per request).
- Context-length: billing is for the tokens processed in the request window (what the model actually attends to). Large stored documents are not billed on ingest unless you call a full-document request; cached/pinned prefixes are eligible for reuse credit.
- Rounding & minimums: default billing quantum is 250 tokens; monthly committed bundles are rounded up to the nearest 1,000 tokens for invoicing. We can reduce the quantum for pilots as noted below.

Worked examples (summary):
1) Single call example — 2,000-token prompt + 300-token generation = 2,300 tokens billed (rounded up to nearest 250 => 2,500 tokens charged).
2) 10,000 short calls example — 10k calls x (avg 150 in + 50 out = 200) = 2,000,000 tokens billed => invoices show token line item 2,000,000 (already multiple of 250, no extra rounding).
3) Long-context access — if you store a 32k doc but the call asks only for a 1,000-token excerpt, we bill for ~1,000 tokens (plus any retrieval tokens spent building the context window). If you stitch multiple excerpts into a single request, those tokens are billed as one request. Prefix caching: if the same 4k prompt prefix is reused across calls, we apply a prefix reuse credit (approx 75% credit on repeated prefix tokens, visible in Console token breakdown).

Pilot concessions we can offer for AcmeHealth:
- Reduce billing quantum from 250 -> 100 tokens for the first 90 days of the pilot.
- Waive the monthly minimum floor for the pilot month (no minimum invoice), after which standard minimums apply.
- Committed token true-up: unused committed tokens in a billing month can roll forward as credit for up to 90 days.

I'll attach the PDF with line-item math and the XLSX with price tiers for your review. If this looks good I can update the SOW to reflect the pilot concessions.

Attachment: proposed_pricing_table_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48K)
Attachment: token_amortization_examples.pdf (application/pdf, 35K)

Best,
Karthik
Head of Strategic GTM — Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: streaming & multi-pass retrieval billing

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from Engineering/Finance:

1) Streaming: for long streaming generations (e.g., a 6,000-token completion streamed back in chunks) does Redwood bill on final total tokens only or are intermediate chunks billed as separate events that could trigger additional rounding?

2) Multi-pass retrieval: our vector search layer may do two retrieval passes — coarse then fine — and then assemble a single prompt. Is each retrieval counted separately or only the assembled prompt+completion?

We want to ensure the pilot won't have hidden rounding inflation if engineering does a multi-pass read/stream pattern.

Thanks,
Tom
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <procure@acmehealth.com>, Lara Chen <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: streaming & multi-pass retrieval billing

Tom —

Good clarifications. Short answers: streaming is billed on the final token count (we accumulate token usage server-side and the invoice reflects the total tokens for the completed request). Intermediate chunking does not incur extra rounding steps.

For multi-pass retrieval the billing model counts the tokens included in the assembled prompt that the model actually attends to. If you perform two retrievals and stitch both results into a single prompt body before the API call, we bill that single assembled prompt (no double-charge for the retrievals performed outside the model). If you make separate model calls for each pass, each call is billed individually.

Note on engineering patterns to reduce charge:
- Use prefix caching for repeated context to get reuse credits.
- Prefer server-side unioning of retrievals into one call when latency allows.

I'll update the SOW language to explicitly state: "billing is per completed model call (input+output tokens); streaming is consolidated; external retrievals stitched pre-call are not billed unless they are passed into separate model calls."

Karthik
